source_anchors.purpose: Normal dedicated recovery image construction is preserved in the unselected branch.
Copy the exact signed input with size and SHA256 checks before and after installation.
Keep the exact recovery bytes and omit generated RECOVERY source metadata.
BOOTABLE_IMAGES is returned unchanged before other image sources.
PREBUILT_IMAGES calls _SignBootableImage and must not carry the selected recovery.

limitations: The project commit identifies the reviewed upstream base; matching these files does not attest the entire current source checkout.
The selector requires an independently validated image and expected SHA256. The copy rule preserves signed bytes; it is not an AVB signature or key trust verifier.
Only the selected dedicated recovery image uses this copy path. Normal boot, init_boot, vendor_boot, AVB and rollback rules are unchanged.
The selected target-files branch omits generated RECOVERY files, recovery filesystem metadata and the recovery resource ZIP; it does not validate generated misc_info as TWRP metadata.
Full target-files, OTA and super build goals remain denied by the device integration. Companion image compatibility and future OTA or target-files workflows are not validated by this patch.

Fresh target-files generation also requires recovery-two-step.img in the pinned add_img_to_target_files.py at lines 1033-1036. This patch supplies neither that separately validated image nor a RECOVERY source tree; the complete target-files workflow is unsupported and remains denied.

The real recovery.img target uses normal timestamp dependencies, without a phony prerequisite forbidden by Kati. The recoveryimage and recoveryimage-nodeps entrypoints always run the checked copy; target-files independently verifies the installed image bytes before copying. Direct raw file targets alone do not promise unconditional revalidation.
